newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka chemical poisoning kills 2,500/yr - paper.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka chemical poisoning kills 2,500/yr - paper.

text.p: Some 2,500 Sri Lankans are killed each year by chemical poisoning, the independent Island newspaper said on Tuesday.

The daily quoted Labour Minister John Seneviratne as saying about 25,000 people were admitted to hospital with chemical poisoning annually on the Indian Ocean island, which has a population of just over 18 million.
Seneviratne described the casualty rate as very high and said the poisonings were due mostly to occupational hazards or suicides.
The newspaper quoted the minister as saying Sri Lanka's health and safety regulations might be deficient in their treatment of risk from chemicals.
The country's factory ordinances covering workplace safety dated back to 1942, he said.
